content:
# Baruch Chapter 1 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Baruch 1 (22 verses)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Disagreement 001 — v.3: "in the hearing of" vs. "aloud to"

**EMET:** "in the hearing of Jeconiah"
**LOGOS:** "aloud to Jeconiah"
**PNEUMA:** "to Jeconiah"
**Issue:** Greek eis ta ota = "into the ears of." EMET preserves idiom literally. LOGOS and PNEUMA normalize. Consensus: "aloud to."

---

## Disagreement 002 — v.4: Social class terminology

**EMET:** "mighty ones"
**LOGOS:** "nobles"
**PNEUMA:** "powerful men of the community"
**Issue:** Greek dynastai = rulers/powerful men. EMET is most literal; LOGOS "nobles" most natural; PNEUMA adds "community." Consensus: "nobles."

---

## Disagreement 003 — v.4: "from the least to the greatest" vs. "both small and great"

**EMET:** "from the least to the greatest"
**LOGOS:** "both small and great"
**PNEUMA:** "high and low alike"
**Issue:** Greek apo mikrou heos megalou. Merism of totality. All acceptable; consensus: "both small and great."

---

## Disagreement 004 — v.6: "each according to his power" vs. "each as much as he was able"

**EMET:** "each according to his power"
**LOGOS:** "each as much as he was able to give"
**PNEUMA:** "each person giving what they could afford"
**Issue:** Greek kata tēn dynamin = "according to the power/ability." EMET most literal. PNEUMA adds "afford" (financial nuance). Consensus: "each according to his means."

---

## Disagreement 005 — v.8: Temporal structure of the verse

**EMET:** Embedded clause structure following Greek closely
**LOGOS:** "This was at the time when" — adds interpretive temporal frame
**PNEUMA:** "This was the same occasion when" — further paraphrased
**Issue:** Greek syntax is complex; all agents restructure differently. Consensus follows LOGOS framing.

---

## Disagreement 006 — v.9: "leaders/princes" terminology

**EMET:** "leaders"
**LOGOS:** "princes"
**PNEUMA:** "royal court"
**Issue:** Greek archontes = rulers/princes. LOGOS "princes" more technically accurate. PNEUMA's "royal court" is an interpretive expansion. Consensus: "princes."

---

## Disagreement 007 — v.10: Introduction of the message

**EMET:** "And they said: Behold, we send you money"
**LOGOS:** "They said: Here is money"
**PNEUMA:** "The message they sent said: Here is money"
**Issue:** EMET retains "Behold" (idou). LOGOS and PNEUMA omit. PNEUMA adds "The message they sent said" as clarifying frame. Consensus: "They said: Here is money."

---

## Disagreement 008 — v.11: "as the days of heaven"

**EMET:** "as the days of heaven"
**LOGOS:** "like the days of heaven"
**PNEUMA:** "as long as the heavens last"
**Issue:** Greek hōs hai hēmerai tou ouranou = "as the days of heaven." This idiom (from Deut 11:21) is recognized. PNEUMA's expansion is interpretively correct but loses the allusion. Consensus: "as long as the days of heaven."

---

## Disagreement 009 — v.12: "shadow" vs. "shelter" vs. "protection"

**EMET:** "shadow"
**LOGOS:** "protection"
**PNEUMA:** "shelter"
**Issue:** Greek skia = shadow. The royal-protection idiom of "shadow" deserves preservation as it echoes the OT/ANE metaphor (Ps 91, Lam 4:20). Consensus: "shadow."

---

## Disagreement 010 — v.13: "his anger and his wrath" vs. "his anger and wrath"

**EMET:** "the anger of the Lord and his wrath"
**LOGOS:** "his anger and his wrath"
**PNEUMA:** "His anger has not cooled"
**Issue:** EMET preserves the full noun phrase with "the Lord" in both. LOGOS and SOPHIA condense. PNEUMA paraphrases away the doublet. The doublet (orgē kai thymos) is emphatic; consensus retains both nouns.

---

## Disagreement 011 — v.15: "open shame" vs. "shame of face"

**EMET:** "shame of face"
**LOGOS:** "open shame"
**PNEUMA:** "the ones who should be ashamed"
**Issue:** Greek aischynē prosōpou = "shame of face" — a Hebrew idiom (cf. Dan 9:7-8). EMET preserves it; LOGOS normalizes. Consensus: "open shame" as more intelligible while retaining the confessional register.

---

## Disagreement 012 — v.19: "negligent" vs. "careless"

**EMET:** "negligent in not listening"
**LOGOS:** "careless and have not heeded"
**PNEUMA:** "careless with his voice"
**Issue:** Greek ēmelēsamen = we were careless/negligent. EMET renders the participial construction; LOGOS splits into two clauses. Consensus: "careless and have not listened."

---

## Disagreement 013 — v.20: "calamities" vs. "evils"

**EMET:** "calamities"
**LOGOS:** "evils"
**PNEUMA:** "disasters"
**Issue:** Greek ta kaka = the evils/bad things. "Calamities" (EMET) is more elevated; "evils" (LOGOS) more literal; "disasters" (PNEUMA) most vivid. Consensus: "evils."

---

## Disagreement 014 — v.22: "inclinations" vs. "intentions" vs. "desires"

**EMET:** "inclinations of his own evil heart"
**LOGOS:** "intentions of his own wicked heart"
**PNEUMA:** "desires of an evil heart"
**Issue:** Greek enthymēmata = thoughts/intentions/inclinations. The heart-language echoes Gen 6:5 and Jer 7:24. "Desires" is slightly too volitional; "inclinations" and "intentions" both work. Consensus: "desires of his own wicked heart."
